ImageDescription.value: Golden anemone (Condylactis aurantiaca), Pistol Bay, Paphos, Cyprus. This species of anemone is found only in the Mediterranean Sea in depths of up to 80 metres. The base is attached to a rock, stone or shell and the column immersed in sediment, usually sand or gravel, with only the oral disc and tentacles visible. The oral disc may reach 12 centimetres (4.7 in), the overall diameter with the tentacles spread out is around 30 centimetres (12 in) and each tentacle is around 8 centimetres (3 in) long, green to yellow in colour, and sometimes greyish. They often have bands of white and other colours, and purple tips.

ImageDescription.value: Helmstadt-Bargen, Germany, district Bargen: ceiling of the Roman Catholic Saint Peter and Paul Church, built in 1904 in Gothic Revival style. The paining of the wooden ceiling is astonishing for such a small church and preserved well. At the top a part of the painted organ gallery. The central painting shows the Veil of Veronica and the instruments of the passion; the angel at the bottom holds a banner saying “In the cross is salvation” (quoted from Thomas à Kempis, De imitatione Christi, chapter 12).
